releases.name: AbyssME 0.8.0 Beta 1
releases.body:
AbyssME now brings 24 platforms together on ARM64. The new platform gallery lets you pick a device and browse its games. Turn on **Show platforms without games** to find a new system, install its firmware if needed, and add your first game.

Alongside Java ME, Mophun, Symbian and N-Gage, the ARM64 edition includes WIPI / SKVM, Dingoo A320, Gemei A330, Aquaplus P/ECE, Watara Supervision, Mega Duck, Cybiko, Flash Lite, Gamate, Palm OS, Palm webOS, Firefox OS, KaiOS, Atari Portfolio, early iPhone OS, Arduboy / FX, Gamebuino Classic, Pokitto, original Thumby and ESPboy. The ARMv7 edition includes Java ME and Mophun.

**Download** the standard APK for ARM64 or the APK marked **armv7** for a 32-bit ARM device. Both require Android 10 or later. Install over the previous official APK to keep your games and saves. Supply your own games and system files.

[Setup guide](https://abysstail.art/guides/abyssme-setup.html) · [Source and build instructions](https://github.com/EriArk/JavaEmulator/blob/v0.8.0-beta.1/docs/releases/v0.8.0-beta.1.md)

releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 10
releases.body:
# AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 10

Beta 10 adds **global physical-controller profiles** and improves Mophun sound and game speed.

Open **Settings → Physical controller profiles** to edit the global mapping or create reusable profiles for buttons and both sticks. Assign them to games from the manager or each game's Controls page. Graphics, touch layouts and physical mappings stay independent. Existing per-game overrides take priority; shared changes apply the next time the game opens. Profiles are included in library backups.

Mophun sound is now enabled for every game. Short BEEP effects and `vBeep` are supported, and PCM follows pause and emulation speed. A common phone-model execution budget reduces excessive speed in CPU-dependent games such as the supplied Boulder Dash and Lemtris versions.

- **ARM64:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.10.apk` — Java ME, Mophun and experimental Symbian/N-Gage.
- **ARMv7:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.10-armv7.apk` — Java ME and Mophun, without Symbian.

Android 10+ is required. Both update the existing app in place. Back up important saves before updating or switching architecture. Source bundles and SHA-256 checksums are included.

releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 9
releases.body:
Beta 9 adds **independent right-stick mapping** for physical controllers.

Open **Controls → Controller mapping → Sticks** to assign the right stick’s directions and diagonals to phone keys, soft keys or Fire. **Identify** detects right-stick movement; pressing R3 remains a separate input. Bindings are saved per game, and existing profiles keep their settings with the new directions unbound.

The shared input path supports Java ME, Mophun and Symbian/N-Gage. This maps stick directions to digital keys; it does not add proportional analog camera support to games.

- **ARM64:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.9.apk` — Java ME, Mophun and experimental Symbian/N-Gage.
- **ARMv7:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.9-armv7.apk` — Java ME and Mophun, without Symbian.

Android 10+ is required. Both update the existing app in place.

Tested with automated input and a virtual joystick on Retroid; physical dual-stick hardware testing remains pending. Source bundles and SHA-256 checksums are included.

releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 8
releases.body:
Beta 8 fixes Lara's black/striped appearance and loading-screen text showing through her model in **Tomb Raider: Underworld 3D**. The cause was incorrect transparency when transferring M3G rendering to the Java ME screen.

Startup errors now show the original game exception instead of only `InvocationTargetException`.

- **ARM64:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.8.apk` — Java ME, Mophun and the combined Symbian runtime.
- **ARMv7:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.8-armv7.apk` — Java ME and Mophun, without Symbian.

Both require Android 10+ and update the existing app without uninstalling.

The reported **Crash Titans 1.3.7 Sony S700i JAR** was also checked. Its code and packed resources are inconsistent; the same reader fails on ordinary Java outside AbyssME. This release does not make that particular JAR playable.

Checks: 427 JVM tests per build, focused Retroid renderer tests, signed APK update and first-room checks. This is not complete-game acceptance. Source bundles and SHA-256 checksums are included.

releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 7
releases.body:
# AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 7

## Separate graphics and control profiles

- **Settings → Graphics profiles** and **Settings → Control profiles** now have
  independent global defaults, named profiles and assignments. Each game can
  select one graphics profile and one control profile. Changing or resetting
  one category leaves the other intact; extra Gamepad buttons remain available.
- Graphics profiles include supported scaling, smoothing, built-in xBRZ/CRT,
  FSR/sharpness, interpolation, LCD filters and capture settings. Java GPU and
  Mophun support GPU effects; Symbian uses its supported host display options.
  Integer scaling falls back to Fit on Symbian. Java-only geometry options are
  identified in the editor's support information.
- Beta 6 combined profiles split automatically: LCD inheritance and exceptions
  move to graphics, while touch settings remain in controls. Other existing
  graphics remain explicit overrides. Reset the relevant category's overrides
  when you want existing games to inherit a shared setup.
- Both catalogs, including unassigned profiles, travel through library backups.
  Phone backups retain portable game definitions. Picture Keep/Undo preserves

releases.name: v1.2.0
releases.body:
It is my pleasure to announce a new version of Hades!

There's a ton of new and exciting features on this one, I'm happy it's finally landing in your hands 😁. 

Among others, this release provides:

## **Highlights**:
- **Cheat code support**:  with all three major cheat devices: GameShark, CodeBreaker and Pro Action Replay v3 (PARv3)
- **xBRZ scaling filter**, for sharp, smooth visuals at high resolutions
- **Idle loop elimination**, to boost the performances of some of your favorite games

## **Emulation**:
- **ROM Mirroring support**, which fixes a bunch of input issues in the Classic NES Series games
- **OBJ rendering cycle limits**: sprites now have a per-scanline rendering budget, like the real PPU
- **PSG channels 2 and 3** are now resampled correctly each time their frequency changes
- **New color correction profiles** based on the work of Pokefan531 and Hunterk

## **Performance**:
- The scheduler now uses a **min-heap** to find the next event faster, giving a significant performance boost
- **Link-time optimizations (LTO)** are now enabled by default for release builds
- Fixed a performance issue when a file dialog was open

### Español
- **Soporte para 2 mandos locales en Android:** Jugador 1 y Jugador 2 independientes por `InputDevice` ID (`read_pad` / `read_pad2`) con detección automática de conexión/desconexión vía JNI.

- **Diagonales en mando físico y reflejos:** Zona muerta radial 2D para alcanzar el 100% en diagonales y `VK_IMAGE_CREATE_CUBE_COMPATIBLE_BIT` en texturas `2D_ARRAY` cuadradas de `6n` capas.

---

### English
- **2-player local controller support on Android:** Independent P1/P2 mapping by `InputDevice` ID (`read_pad` / `read_pad2`) with automatic connect/disconnect tracking.
- **Android 10 (API 29) crash fix:** Guarded `InsetsController` behind API >= 30 with safe legacy immersive fallback.
- **Physical stick diagonals & cubemaps:** 2D radial deadzone for full 100% diagonal reach and `VK_IMAGE_CREATE_CUBE_COMPATIBLE_BIT` on square `6n`-layer `2D_ARRAY` images.

releases.name: v0.3.7: Battle cut-ins & two-sided stencil rendering fix
releases.body:
## Persona 4 Arena Ultimax for Android v0.3.7

### Fixes & Improvements / Correcciones y mejoras
- **Battle Cut-ins Missing Fixed (Fixes #4):**
  Fixed missing special move, super attack, and Persona summon cut-in portraits and animations in battle.
  - Implemented proper two-sided stencil dynamic state (reference, compare mask, and write mask).
  - Added support for \VK_FORMAT_D24_UNORM_S8_UINT\ and \VK_FORMAT_D16_UNORM_S8_UINT\ in dynamic rendering pipelines, enabling stencil writes on all mobile GPUs.
  - Added state invalidation on pass end (\g_bound = Bound{}\) so dynamic stencil state is correctly bound in every render pass.
  *Se corrigió la ausencia de los cut-ins de personajes, ataques especiales e invocaciones de Persona en combate. Se reparó el estado dinámico de stencil de doble cara, el soporte para formatos D24S8/D16S8 en Dynamic Rendering y la invalidación de estado al terminar pases.*

Install over the previous version; your saves and data stay. / Instálalo encima de la versión anterior; tus partidas y datos se mantienen.

releases.body:
## Def Jam Android v1.4 — The Big Update

### Geração de quadros experimental

- Adicionamos **Lossless / LSFG** e **Win-FG** ao modo Vulkan nativo. O LSFG pode atuar nos menus, nas cenas e nas lutas. O Win-FG fica restrito às lutas.

- O contador de FPS tem texto claro. O limite de 45 FPS foi removido.

### Modo de emulação hakuX

- O launcher agora oferece **Vulkan nativo** e **hakuX**.
- O **hakuX 1.3.0** integrado é uma opção para testar quando o port nativo não funciona no seu aparelho. O emulador exige Android ARM64 e um driver Vulkan com os recursos necessários, então a compatibilidade varia.
- Ao usar a pasta extraída do seu próprio jogo, o launcher pode preparar e reutilizar uma XISO temporária para o emulador.
- Créditos da emulação a **rfandango e aos colaboradores do hakuX**, e ao **projeto xemu** pelo áudio MCPX/APU. O hakuX é distribuído sob GPL-3.0 ou posterior. As fontes do núcleo, dependências

releases.name: Def Jam v1.3 — Discord, Voice & Controls Update
releases.body:
Def Jam v1.3 brings Discord account integration, room discovery corrections, voice chat, refreshed menus and restored custom analog controls to the Android ARM64 port.

## Online and Discord
- Sign in through the official FFNY Online Discord account service. New connections use the verified account name; the manual player-name screen is removed.
- Saved sessions use encrypted app-private storage. Account sign-out, deletion and privacy controls remain accessible inside the game.
- Fixed the PC build fingerprint used for ordinary room and player discovery. The missing build-number bytes previously separated Android players from compatible PC lobbies.
- Choose Europe or North America from the launcher. Both players must use the same region.
- Added real account statistics and leaderboard access in the native online menu.
- Preserved room codes, native room creation, fighter selection and the existing online flow.

## Room voice chat
- Added PC-compatible room voice with push-to-talk: enable voice, allow microphone access and hold MIC to speak.
- Added a microphone permission prompt on first game entry, playback volume and a Mute/Unmute microphone button.

releases.name: Def Jam v1.2 — Controls & Compatibility Update
releases.body:
Update for the Android ARM64 port, focused on controls, frame pacing and online compatibility.

## Changes since v1.1
- Expanded Xbox/PlayStation-style and custom touch control layouts, including dual analog input and editable menu buttons.
- Improved the online player-name prompt and retained the original in-game online menu with room codes. Removed the extra floating ONLINE shortcut; Enter/Start is retained.
- Updated automatic 60 FPS menu / 30 FPS low-end combat pacing, frame-time statistics and CPU/network diagnostics. Actual performance depends on the device and scene.
- Reduced repeated missing-file lookups and refined online input waiting and delay handling.
- Updated the public relay connection handshake and corrected misleading password errors and repeated connection attempts after rejection.
- Included experimental, opt-in rollback support. It is not certified for stable cross-device play and respects the relay's rollback permission.

Existing saves, the built-in ISO/XISO extractor, gamepad support, English/Portuguese/Spanish interfaces and asynchronous Vulkan rendering are retained.

## Important online notice

releases.name: xbased 1.2.16
releases.body:
## 1.2.16 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- Psi-Ops: The Mindgate Conspiracy (Europe) went to a black screen after the
  opening cinematics of a new game, in every language (#444). The game frees
  its text file as a new game starts and loads it again into a block of the
  same size, and it keeps using a pointer into the old block, so it needs
  that block back at the same address. Small blocks the emulator's kernel
  made in between took that spot. They now fill a gap instead, the block
  comes back where it was and the game goes on into the first level.
- Chase: Hollywood Stunt Driver could crash as its first loading screen came
  up when its cache drive had last been used by another game. After the
  drive was formatted the emulator still reported the other game's files as
  using the space, so the game found no room and no file of its own to
  delete. A format and a deleted file now show in the free space at once.
- Alter Echo: the movie at the start of a new game stayed on its first
  frame while its sound played, since 1.2.0 (#197). The movie's picture sits
  in the memory of an older frame, and the emulator kept the copy it made

releases.name: xbased 1.2.15
releases.body:
## 1.2.15 (2026-11)

### Performance
- Games that read the picture they are drawing as a texture, as Riddick's
  lighting does about 150 times a frame, no longer copy the whole picture
  before each of those draws. The picture is read where it is drawn. The
  copies weigh most on cards with little memory speed: in Escape from
  Butcher Bay a GTX 1050 at 2x dropped to 35-50 fps, and a fast card at 6x
  went from 50 to 60 fps in the same scene (#435).

### Fixes
- Chronicles of Riddick froze a few seconds into a new game, and in some
  later chapters, on slower graphics cards since 1.2.14. The emulator let a
  game run further ahead of the graphics card than an Xbox does, and Riddick
  ended up with more visibility tests waiting than it has room for. Now a
  game is at most a frame ahead of what the card has drawn, as on the
  console. A card that keeps up never waits (#435).
- Blade II: the characters' shadows were pale pink streaks on the street
  again, since 1.2.0 (#287). When a vertex program writes no fog, the Xbox's
  graphics chip uses the fog its earlier vertices left (it keeps the last 6),
  and xbased gave those vertices no fog distance, so the city's haze coloured

releases.name: xbased 1.2.14
releases.body:
## 1.2.14 (2026-11)

### Performance
- Scenes made of many small pieces run much faster. A game that draws lots
  of small triangle strips one after another has them drawn as one, and each
  draw uploads only the shader constants it uses. 007 Everything or
  Nothing's first level, looking at the courtyard, went from 38 to about 135
  fps uncapped on a fast PC, and at Original it now holds 30 where it
  dropped to 13 (#429).
- Interrupts reach the emulated CPU with a single memory write instead of a
  call into Windows, which made every game's interrupts cheaper.
- Uncapped games that show a frame every second vblank no longer wait on
  Windows' timer between the two, which can't wait less than half a
  millisecond.
- Unlocked on a 120 Hz or faster display (VRR or not): a frame that comes
  late is shown at once instead of waiting for the display's next refresh.

### Fixes
- Frame rate limit: Spyro A Hero's Tail ran at 64.5 fps at Up to 60. The
  limit followed a vsync grid that slowly moved back, and the display's
  refresh period could be measured as a fraction of the real one. Frames are
  now counted against the display's refreshes (#430).

releases.name: xbased 1.2.13
releases.body:
## 1.2.13 (2026-11)

A cleanup and optimization release: the same emulator, with less code.

### Changes
- The code is cleaned of everything that no longer served: the paths for
  platforms xbased doesn't run on, the workarounds for graphics drivers no PC
  has, old files, and functions nothing called any more. About 8,000 lines of
  code less, the executable a little smaller, and nothing that changes how
  games run.
- Depth buffers are created only with the uses they have, which leaves the
  driver more room to compress them.
- The debug switches (props.ini) are read by one piece of code on Windows and
  Linux alike.
- The source repository is tidier: README, BUILDING and CHANGELOG at its root,
  the build steps in one place, and every library built in listed with its
  license.

### Fixes
- The Linux build compiles without warnings on Ubuntu 22.04 (a few
  declarations its C library doesn't have).

releases.name: xbased 1.2.12
releases.body:
## 1.2.12 (2026-11)

### New
- Downsampling (Settings > Video > Downsampling: Off, 1x, 2x, 4x): the game
  is drawn at the internal resolution, then the picture is averaged down to
  the console's own resolution, or twice or four times it, before it's scaled
  to your screen. Smooth edges with the original look. It needs an internal
  resolution above the size chosen, and works with FXAA, FSR and the CRT look
  (#427).

### Fixes
- Fable The Lost Chapters: the hero's hair could turn into streaks up close
  after some area loads, until the next restart. The game builds the hero's
  look into a cache on the hard disk at each load, and a piece of it drawn
  where a swizzled texture of the same size had been landed in the wrong
  pixel order (#380).
- Savestates: a state made from a .chd loads from an .iso of the same dump
  and the other way round, and a state that is refused says why in the log.
- Frame rate limit: with the GPU maxed out (a high internal resolution on a
  laptop) the frame rate could drift above the limit, 64 fps at Up to 60 in
  Crash Bandicoot The Wrath of Cortex. The moments the presenter picks frames

releases.body:
# v0.0.8.2 Experimental — Stability Update & On-Screen Control Editor

Small stability update on top of `v0.0.7.9-experimental`. Still experimental — please use **EXPORT LOGS** when reporting anything.

## New: customize the on-screen controls

A **CUSTOMIZE** pill now sits next to **TOUCH** in the HUD. It opens an in-place editor:

- Tap a control to select it, then **drag** to move it.
- **S- / S+** resize, **O- / O+** change opacity.
- **BIND** cycles a button's guest input index.
- **PRESET** cycles DEFAULT → COMPACT → LEFT → RIGHT.
- **RESET** restores the original layout, **DONE** saves and exits.

Layouts are stored as normalized coordinates, so they survive rotation/window resizing and app restarts. Guest input is suppressed while the editor is open (no phantom presses), gamepad focus rules are unchanged, and **TOUCH: OFF** also leaves edit mode.

## Stability / rendering correctness (from the in-progress post-0.0.7.9 patch)

- Pixel shaders now use full FP32 with NaN-safe multiply helpers (`mulL`/`mulL1`), clamp-before-scale texture adjustment, and `isnan()` output sanitization — removes FP16 overflow/NaN artifacts without changing the guest shader set.

### Highlights & Fixes

- **Fixed Missing Initial Lighting / Pitch-Black Areas on Boot (No Longer Requires Tapping `RES`)**

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.1.0 (beta)
releases.body:
CapyPS5 0.1.0 is the **first beta**: faster on every game, fewer crashes, and on-screen controls you can lay out yourself. PS4 backward compatibility stays experimental. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**Faster**
- **The GPU thread runs on the fastest CPU cores.** On a Snapdragon 8 Elite this alone made a demanding Unreal Engine 4 level about a third faster.
- **Less waiting for the GPU.** Several cases where the emulator stopped to read back data the GPU had just written are gone:
  - fast-clear metadata fills now run on the CPU;
  - GPU-driven draws of PS4 games are executed on the GPU;
  - fresh buffer data is copied without a system call per page.
  The same level gained about 30 % more on top.
- **Cheaper per-draw work:** shader resource tables are read in one go per table on ARM, which halved the cost of preparing each draw.

**More stable**
- Unreal Engine games that closed with a corrupt memory error a few seconds into a level (the game's own allocator reporting a broken "canary", or a crash reading address 1) no longer do: the emulator stopped waiting for a GPU signal that was only late.

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.6
releases.body:
Sixth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android, and the first with **PS4 backward compatibility**: PS4 games now run in CapyPS5 the way they do on a real PS5. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New: PS4 backward compatibility**

A PS5 runs PS4 games on its own hardware. CapyPS5 does the same in software: PS4 games use the same x86-64 JIT, system libraries and Vulkan renderer as PS5 games, and only what the PS4 does differently was added.
- **GPU:** PS4 (GCN gfx7) shaders and registers, PS4 render targets and texture tiling, CMASK and HTile fast clears, cube and volume textures, and the PS4 Gnm driver calls.
- **System:** PS4 executables and the modules games ship, the PS4 memory layout and flexible memory budget, and PS4 save data and trophies.
- PS4 games go in the same game folders as PS5 games (a folder with `eboot.bin` and `sce_sys/param.sfo`) and carry a **PS4** mark in the library.
- This is the first release with it. 2D and Unity games run best; Unreal Engine 4 games start but are slow; many games don't boot yet. Lower the resolution for big games.

**Also new**

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.5
releases.body:
Fifth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. Mali GPUs on their system driver can now run games, and the FPS counter shows how many frames CapyPS5 Framegen adds. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New**
- **Mali on the system driver:** that driver cannot sample BCn compressed textures, so the GPU used to be rejected. CapyPS5 now decompresses those textures on the GPU when it uploads them (BC1 to BC7, including BC6H HDR textures). GPUs that support BCn keep using it directly.
- **PanVK on Mali:** the GPU is no longer rejected when the driver lacks vertex-stage stores or dual-source blending.
- **Framegen counter:** with CapyPS5 Framegen on, the FPS counter reads *XX FPS - YY FG*: XX are the game's own frames, YY the total including generated ones. The options are now called *Framegen x2*, *x3* and *x4*.
- **HDR10 output:** games that output HDR10 are converted to SDR for the screen.

**Fixed**
- Tessellation: quad domains, fractional-even spacing, counterclockwise output and masked hull control points.

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.4
releases.body:
Fourth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. More than 100 games now run correctly according to testers' reports, and this release adds CapyPS5 Framegen. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New**
- **CapyPS5 Framegen:** optional frame generation. It draws in-between frames from the motion between two game frames, so a game at 30 FPS is shown at 60. Off by default; turn it on in *Settings → Performance* (1 per frame, or up to 3). Adds one frame of latency and some GPU load; works best from 25 FPS up.
- New performance options in *Settings → Performance*: shadow resolution, early depth testing and a frame rate limit (30 or 20 FPS).
- Physical keyboard input and an on-screen keyboard toggle for text fields, and system dialogs that can now be answered.
- Android 16 and devices with 16 KB memory pages are supported.

**Fixed**
- Unreal Engine 5 games: graphics and async compute hand work back and forth several times per frame, and each hand-off waited up to 100 ms. Menus that ran at 0–2 FPS now move.
- Games whose shadows use depth-compare texture gathers (Castlevania: Belmont's Curse) closed after the menu.

releases.name: Castlevania port v0.5.0
releases.body:
## No more blinking objects after loading

While the game is running, each new combination of shader and render state needs a GPU pipeline. Pipelines the app has never seen are built in the background so the game doesn't freeze, and until one is ready the objects that use it are not drawn. Until now that also happened to pipelines it had already built in an earlier session. Only the first 4,000 were prepared at start-up, in the order they first appeared, so later in the game whole areas came from the background again. The result was objects and textures blinking for a few frames after loading a save or when walking into an area.

- Pipelines that the app has already built on your device are now created on the spot, in about a quarter of a millisecond each and within a small per-frame budget, so they are drawn from the first frame.
- Start-up preparation now begins with the pipelines your last session used (`pipelines_recientes.bin` in the game folder), not with the ones from the beginning of the game.
- Areas you visit for the very first time can still show an object a moment late while its pipeline is built. The second visit is clean.

releases.body:
**This is a test build, not a release.** It is for [issue 39](https://github.com/JackandBeans/Snap64Recomp/issues/39): on a phone with an Exynos 2400, the Android app shows the same graphics message at every start once Anti-Aliasing is set to 8x. Everyone else should use [1.1.7](https://github.com/JackandBeans/Snap64Recomp/releases/tag/v1.1.7).

It is the code that will become 1.1.8, as it stands today. When the phone cannot make a picture buffer at the settings chosen, the port lowers a setting and asks for a restart. 1.1.7 only ever lowered Super Sampling, so with Super Sampling already at 1x nothing changed and every start ended the same way. This build lowers one setting each time: Super Sampling, then Anti-Aliasing, then Color Depth, then Render Scale. It never asks for an Anti-Aliasing level the phone does not offer, it remembers a level that failed, and the log names the levels the phone offers.

Install it over 1.1.7. Saves stay. If 1.1.7 left the phone stuck, the first start of this build should lower Anti-Aliasing to 4x by itself and get into the game. If it still stops, attach `snap64.log` from Internal storage > Snap64 to issue 39.

releases.body:
**This is a test build, not a release.** It is for the crash in [issue 36](https://github.com/JackandBeans/Snap64Recomp/issues/36): on an AYN Thor, the Android app closes as the game starts. Everyone else should use [1.1.7](https://github.com/JackandBeans/Snap64Recomp/releases/tag/v1.1.7).

It is [1.1.7-test3](https://github.com/JackandBeans/Snap64Recomp/releases/tag/v1.1.7-test3) with a fix for the crash that build recorded. The Thor's graphics driver crashed at the end of the first drawing pass of the first frame. That pass held a reset of the renderer's timers, which Vulkan does not allow inside a drawing pass. The port's own clear of new picture buffers had left the pass open. Now the reset, and the two other steps Vulkan keeps outside a drawing pass, close an open pass first. The log says so once.

The crash record from test3 stays in. If the app still closes, open it once more, then attach `snap64.log` to issue 36. Saves stay.

releases.name: v0.1.9-alpha
releases.body:
### Fixed

- The Linux release plays game movies: it links a small static FFmpeg (FFmpeg's own H.264, HEVC, VP8/VP9, AAC, Opus, Vorbis and MP3 decoders, no other libraries), so it needs no FFmpeg on the system and works whatever FFmpeg version the distribution has. The 0.1.8 archive was built without FFmpeg, and Astro Bot crashed at its first movie (#7).

releases.name: v0.1.8-alpha
releases.body:
### Changed

- The emulated display is 1080p by default (it was 2160p), in the launcher, `rps5e-cli run` and the test scripts: games that size their output to the display render a quarter of the pixels and the window scales the picture, which is much lighter on the GPU. 2160p (and 720p) stay selectable in the launcher's settings, per game, and with `--display-resolution` / `RPS5E_DISPLAY_RESOLUTION`. Games that do not ask for the display's resolution are shown a 2160p display as on the console.
- System functions answer as measured on a PS5 in a game process: a trylock of an adaptive mutex by its owner returns EINVAL (was EBUSY); `sceKernelAddAmprEvent` on a deleted or null event queue returns EBADF (was success); `sceSystemServiceReceiveEvent` with no event pending returns "no event" for any pointer and leaves the buffer untouched (it wrote an empty event first, and a null pointer was a parameter error); the `sceNetGetSockInfo` record carries the socket priority 0x10.
- `sceVideoOutSetFlipRate` checks the handle before the rate and accepts rate 3 (a flip every fourth vblank), as on a PS5.

releases.name: 0.1.7-alpha - 2026-11-13
releases.body:
### Fixed

- Ghost of Yōtei no longer freezes after its shaders are compiled (#3). Two causes:
  - Planning the resources of a shader walked the shader's whole value graph again for every word of every buffer descriptor; on this game's largest shaders that took minutes on the GPU command thread, with nothing submitted meanwhile. Each value is now walked once per shader.
  - A few compute shaders became SPIR-V modules of 2.7-3.2 million words that the GPU driver compiled for 15 minutes and more while the game waited (the driver keeps the result, so only the first run on a machine stalled). The largest is now 0.6 million words and builds in about 40 s on an RTX 5090, once; the results are the same, bit for bit (device tests over every buffer format, page-crossing elements and partial EXEC):

releases.name: 0.1.6-alpha - 2026-11-12
releases.body:
### Fixed

- Windows: controllers work out of the box. The release archive now carries `SDL3.dll`: the emulator loads SDL at run time and Windows has none of its own, so no controller was found ("SDL3 not available") unless the file was added by hand. The message for a missing library now says where to put it ([#4](https://github.com/keklick1337/rps5e/issues/4)).


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/keklick1337/rps5e/compare/v0.1.5-alpha...v0.1.6-alpha

releases.name: 1.0.5-alpha
releases.body:
### Changed

- The automatic choice of the recording thread (`RPS5E_GPU_RECORD_THREAD=auto`) no longer turns it off while the command interpreter also has to wait for room in its queue (`RPS5E_POLICY_FULL`). SILENT HILL: The Short Message's heavy room about 10 fps instead of 8; GTA V with `RPS5E_BDA=1` 47 fps instead of 42.
- `RPS5E_BDA=1` (experimental direct guest memory reads) no longer changes the default of `RPS5E_LABELS_AT_EOP`: with its old default (`1`) GTA V never left its start menu. GTA V's city in Performance mode with `RPS5E_BDA=1`: 47-48 fps against 37 without it; still off by default.
- The emulator's own small writes into GPU-watched guest memory (memcpy/memset inside one page, packets of the command-buffer builders) mark the page written before the store instead of taking a page fault (`RPS5E_PREMARK_SMALL`). GTA V's city in Performance mode: write faults per frame ~1550 → ~320; over the same stretch of the scene the frame rate rises by about 2.5 % (36.6 → 37.4 fps).

releases.name: v2.0.1
releases.body:
v2.0.1 release of Skate 3 Recomp for Windows, Linux, and macOS (ARM / Experimental).

A stability and hygiene patch for v2.0.0, focused on the crash and antivirus reports from the first few hours.

## Downloads

- Windows: `Skate3Recomp-Windows.zip`
- Linux: `Skate3Recomp-Linux.zip`
- macOS: `Skate3Recomp-macOS.zip`

## Changes

#### Stability

- Fixed a crash on Linux and macOS where the game could die suddenly during gameplay when world streaming revoked memory the renderer was reading
- Fixed distant demoted tree trunks rendering with a flat blue texture

#### Antivirus false positives

- The Windows executable and runtime DLL now carry proper version metadata, and the runtime no longer contains any ability to create executable memory (it never used it - all game code is compiled at build time); both changes target the machine-learning heuristics some antivirus engines were tripping on
- A false-positive report has been filed with Microsoft for the v2.0.0 files; if your antivirus quarantined the runtime, restore it or re-download this release

#### Diagnostics

- The game now logs its exact build version at startup, so support logs identify the build they came from

releases.body:
Use the new v2.0.2 release for critical fixes.

v2.0.0 release of Skate 3 Recomp for Windows, Linux, and macOS (ARM / Experimental).

Skate 3 now renders natively. This release replaces the emulated Xbox 360 GPU with a new renderer built directly on Direct3D 12 and Vulkan: more than double the frame rate at around a quarter of the GPU power draw, and on macOS a jump from roughly 25 FPS to 250 FPS at 4K. The entire game renders natively at close visual parity with the console output, with a set of optional modern graphics enhancements that seek to go beyond it.

The new native renderer is early and is likely to have issues, I haven't tested the game all the way through.

## Downloads

- Windows: `Skate3Recomp-Windows.zip`
- Linux: `Skate3Recomp-Linux.zip`
- macOS: `Skate3Recomp-macOS.zip`

## Changes

#### Native renderer

- New native renderer on Direct3D 12 and Vulkan, enabled by default, replacing the emulated Xbox 360 GPU
- More than 2x the frame rate at about a quarter of the GPU power draw; macOS goes from ~25 FPS to ~250 FPS (at 4K render scaling, excluding the optional enhancements like PCSS shadows)

releases.body:
# Open Nectar 1.0.9.1 — Windows antivirus fix

### **Windows only.** 

Linux, macOS and Android stay on
[1.0.9](https://github.com/SSunnKing/Open-Nectar---Pikmin-Native-PC-Mobile-Port/releases/tag/1.0.9).
Download those from there. Nothing changes in the games themselves.

**Updating:** press **Update** in your launcher. Saves, settings and texture
packs carry over.

## Windows Defender flagged the launcher as a trojan

Some players got a "Threat found" warning from Windows Defender for
`nectar-launcher.exe` (`Trojan:Win32/Bearfoos.A!ml`). This was a false
positive. The `!ml` means it came from Defender's machine-learning guess,
not from a real malware match.

The launcher was doing things that look suspicious to an antivirus: it
started `curl.exe` and `tar.exe` in the background to download updates and
texture packs, and the exe had no publisher or version info. This release
changes that:

* Downloads now happen inside the launcher instead of through `curl.exe`.
* Update zips are unpacked inside the launcher instead of through `tar.exe`.
* `nectar.exe`, `nectar-pal.exe` and `nectar-launcher.exe` now have
  publisher and version information (right-click → Properties → Details).

Fourteenth beta of KINGDOM HEARTS 358/2 Days for Android on **[khdays-port 0.1.5](https://github.com/Yokimitsuro/khdays-port/releases/tag/v0.1.5)**, Yokimitsuro's native PC port that this Android version follows. All the credit for the port itself goes there.

## What's new since beta 13

- **No more flicker in the camera's crossfades on Mali graphics chips** (AYANEO Pocket Air Mini and other Mali devices). In a cutscene's crossfade between two camera shots, some pictures showed the new shot with blocks of the old one in it, and the fade went back and forth. The graphics driver ran two steps of the picture in the wrong order; they are now done in a way it keeps in order.
- **No pause in the middle of a cutscene when a KH2 model with moving cloth first appears** (with the HD PACK). The first such model's cloth used to be prepared on the spot, about a sixth of a second; all of them are now prepared in the background while the title shows.

releases.name: v2.2.0
releases.body:
## New since v2.1.6 (last stable)

- **Steam ISO manual export** — Steam ISO files (`<Game Name>.iso` to `Downloads/front end/`) are no longer written automatically on every game list load. They are now written on demand via the **FileDownload** (↓) button in the My Games top bar, preventing unnecessary writes and duplicate file churn.
- **ISO duplicate skip** — ISO export now checks if the file already exists in `Downloads/front end/` before writing; skips silently if it does, preventing duplicate entries.
- **Game name sanitization** — Game names are sanitized before being used in MediaStore queries and ISO file creation (colons and other illegal filename characters are replaced), fixing a crash/failure when Steam game names contain colons or other special characters.

---

## Full Feature Set

**Core**
- No root required — uses Android's Storage Access Framework (SAF) for secure folder access.
- Single data/ grant — one SAF permission at `<package>/data` covers components, virtual containers, and shadercache simultaneously.
- Multi-app support — automatically detects all installed GameHub variants side by side.

releases.name: v2.1.9-pre
releases.body:
Move Steam ISO export from automatic (every load) to a manual button.

The download arrow (⬇) button appears in the My Games top bar when an app is selected and Steam games are loaded. Tapping it writes/updates the ISOs for all Steam games on demand.

Navigation is now instant — no more SteamRepository.fetch() + MediaStore operations firing silently on every tab visit.

releases.name: v2.1.8-pre
releases.body:
Fix Counter-Strike: Source (and any game with : in the name) creating a new ISO every launch.

**Root cause:** Steam game names with colons (e.g. `Counter-Strike: Source`) get stored in MediaStore with the colon replaced by `_`. The existence check queried with the original name (colon), found nothing, and inserted again — MediaStore then auto-renamed the new file to `Counter-Strike_ Source (1).iso`, `(2).iso`, etc.

**Fix:** Sanitize filename chars `[/\\:*?"<>|]` → `_` before any MediaStore query or insert, so both sides always agree on the name.

releases.name: v2.1.7-pre
releases.body:
Fix duplicate ISO files in Downloads/front end/ on every app launch.

**Root cause:** The old code called MediaStore delete() then insert() each launch. On Android, delete() removes the catalog entry but not the physical file — so insert() would see the file already on disk and auto-rename it to `Counter-Strike_ Source (1).iso`, `(2).iso`, etc.

**Fix:** Query first. If the ISO already exists, skip writing it entirely. No duplicates.

- No root required — uses Android Storage Access Framework (SAF)
- Single `data/` grant per app covers components, virtual containers, and shadercache

releases.name: v2.0.0
releases.body:
Dusklight 2.0 is here! This update brings **mod support**, **an in-game mod browser**, and **our own built-in randomizer**, alongside more polish, performance improvements, and ways to play. Thank you to everyone who helped make it happen!

## Mods and built-in mods

- **Added:** Mod support! Install gameplay mods, asset replacements, and texture packs as `.dusk` bundles, and manage them from the Mods menu. (Modders: check out our [modding documentation](https://github.com/TwilitRealm/dusklight/blob/main/docs/modding.md)!)
- **Added:** An in-game mod browser: search for mods, view information and screenshots, and download and install without leaving Dusklight.
- **Added:** Mod update checks, release notes, and a quick way to update all mods.
- **Added:** Drag and drop `.dusk` mods onto the Dusklight window to install them.
- **Added:** Enable, disable, and reload mods in-game, with dependency handling and per-mod settings and logs.
- **Added:** Built-in Dusklight Randomizer, our own randomizer with seed generation, settings presets, shareable
  permalinks, and more.

releases.body:
Scheduler and file I/O fixes from upstream Xenia Edge: file reads and writes finish the way they do on the console, and kernel timers and DPCs behave like the console's.

Halo: Reach runs much faster and shows the characters' faces again: from 17 to its limit of 30 fps in the first mission on a POCO F7 (Adreno 825).

Gears of War 3 returns to its 30 fps cap in its opening checkpoint on a POCO F7 (Adreno 825), cutting GPU frame time by 37% (44.9 to 28.2 ms).

Game folder management after initial setup, a 40 FPS frame rate cap for 120 Hz displays, lower power draw and heat on Android, and improved physical controller trigger and remapping support.

Upstream Xenia Edge synchronization (batch 16) bringing 40 audio, kernel, scheduler, threading and CPU fixes, plus an ARMv8.0 JIT fix for older Snapdragon chips.

Improves Vulkan startup compatibility on older Adreno GPUs, ports rendering accuracy fixes from Xenia Edge, and reduces vertex shader overhead when software round-toward-zero emulation is active.

# YukiHub v0.4.5 更新日志

> 本次更新聚焦：**四平台游玩状态同步 · Hikarinagi 快捷登录优化 · SD 卡目录授权 · 稳定性修复**

## ✨ 全新功能

- **同步游玩状态至四个平台**：现在可以把本地的游玩时长与进度，一键同步到 **NextMoe·未萌（鲲 Galgame）**、**VNDB**、**Bangumi** 与 **Hikarinagi**。四个平台的入口统一收进个人资料页的「同步游玩状态」折叠卡，点开后按平台逐项操作，状态一目了然。
- **Hikarinagi 快捷登录支持邮箱识别**：现在用 Hikarinagi 快捷登录时会一并读取邮箱，若该邮箱已在 YukiHub 注册过，**将直接登录并绑定到原账号**，与 NextMoe·未萌 的行为完全一致，不再另开新号、云同步数据也不会分裂。

## 🎨 体验优化

- **内置 Gal 工具箱常规维护**：同步更新内置工具箱里的网址与内容，保持可用。
- **同步进度弹窗重做**：进度展示改为环形进度 + 分步状态，四个平台的同步过程都能清楚看到当前在做什么。
- **新增取消绑定游玩状态同步凭证**:打开对应窗口后，长按即可弹出取消，清空凭证以重新登陆。
- **bangumi游戏自定义查询新增id查询**:因api缺陷，部分游戏不能直接搜到，因此新增了id搜索，在自定义搜索界面，直接输入数字is即可。

## 🛠 问题修复

- **修复 NextMoe 源封面模糊的问题**：部分作品封面会取到低分辨率图，现已修正取图逻辑。
- **修复通知权限疯狂弹窗的问题**：此前会反复请求通知权限，现已正常。
- **修复 SD 卡授权时选不到指定文件夹的问题**：内置文件选择器新增 SD 卡支持，现在可以正常选中 SD 卡里的游戏目录。

## 📌 说明

- **同步范围**：VNDB 不支持通过 API 写入游玩时长，因此同步到 VNDB 时只同步状态。
- **首次同步需要授权**：各平台同步需先在对应平台完成一次授权，之后会在后台自动使用。
- **Hikarinagi 登录**：已用旧方式登录过的老账号不受影响，仍会登录原来的账号；新登录会自动识别邮箱。
- **升级不影响存档**：本次更新不涉及引擎与存档逻辑，原有存档数据可正常读取。

---

感谢每一位玩家的反馈与支持，祝游玩愉快！🎮

## What this release fixes · 本版修复

**EN**

- Porting some games stopped at the "GLSLC capture" stage with a build error
  and produced nothing (Eastward and Tokyo Xanadu eX+ were reported). The
  capture works again: games that compile their shaders at run time port
  through now.
- Pressing "Update runtime" on a game's page rebuilt the runtime without the
  game's per-build tables, and Unreal-engine games crashed at startup
  afterwards (FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE, Octopath Traveler 0, DRAGON QUEST VII
  Reimagined). The rebuild carries the game's full build data now.
- The build page's progress reads correctly, and installing a game no longer
  retranslates every shader (@mijuu, #79).

**Before you update**: your games keep the runtime they have and play exactly
as before — the fixes take effect when you port again or press "Update
runtime". If a game of yours crashes at startup after a rebuild, press it once
more after updating: the game starts, and your saves were never at risk.

**中文**

- 一些游戏的移植停在"GLSLC capture"阶段并报构建错误、没有产物(已收到
  Eastward 与 Tokyo Xanadu eX+ 的报告)。现在可以正常通过:运行时自己编译
  着色器的游戏能移植了。
- 在游戏页面点"Update runtime"重建运行库时会丢掉游戏的 per-build 数据表,

### The assistant is in the app

The app carries an assistant now. It runs on the phone itself, in the same
Linux environment the porting tools run in, so no computer is involved. Ask
it in your own words - why a game crashed, why a port would not build, what
is in the library - and it reads the game's log, the build's output and the
library's state by itself. It answers in the language you write to it.

A game that misbehaves goes to a case worker: it opens a case file for that
game - the symptom, the cause, the fix it proposes - and its steps are
visible while it works. A code change waits until you say yes. The knowledge
it diagnoses with ships inside the app: over 400 upstream porting cases,
sorted by what you see, searchable and offline.

To talk to a model the assistant needs one of your own: the Settings tab
takes a provider, a model and a key, and the key stays on the phone.
Without a key, everything else in the app works exactly as before.

### Porting on the phone

A merged dump - one file holding the base game, its update and the DLC
together - now ports as its own version; it could pick the wrong patch or

### The gamepad and the touch stick

The face buttons of a controller are one choice now: by position (the Switch's
layout - X on top, Y on the left, A on the right, B at the bottom) or by what
the controller prints. It is set per controller in the gamepad center and takes
effect at once. The per-key rebinding is gone: it needed a capture flow and a
binding table, players got lost in it, and a rebound button took another key's
source away without anyone seeing why. The center's scope shows what the game
receives, so pressing a button is the test.

The controller's axes are read the way that controller reports them. The Xbox
family (a USB xpad, a Bluetooth XInput pad) puts its triggers on Z/RZ and its
right stick on RX/RY - the opposite of the usual layout - so those pads'
triggers never fired and their right stick never reached the game. The app now
works the roles out of the device's own ranges.

The touch stick starts where the thumb lands: the offset is taken from the
point the finger went down, so a thumb on the rim has output right away. A
small dead zone around that point, the rim is the full deflection, and the
right stick is finer at low speed.

## Before you update · 更新之前(必读)

- (EN) This build fixes the runtime build on the phone. If you have not imported the profiles package of v0.4.0-alpha01 yet, you still must: the app runs the games on the new host (0.4.0), and the old package's packs were built for the previous one. Import it in the environment check (the "manage" box).
- (中文) 本版修复了手机上的运行库构建。如果你还没有导入 v0.4.0-alpha01 的档案包，现在仍然必须导入：App 用新宿主(0.4.0)运行游戏，旧档案包的数据包是按旧宿主构建的。到环境检查里(那个"管理"按钮)导入。

## Fixed: the runtime a game needs on the phone builds again

The new host (0.4.0) checks every profile's picture - the screenshot the README shows - and looked for it in the app's own tool folder, where the pictures are not shipped: the build failed with "readme_image 'docs/images/...': no such file in the repository", and every game whose profile names a picture could not be rebuilt. The check now runs where the pictures are (a checkout of the repository), and the app's own copy leaves it out. Sixty games had a picture in their profile: all of them build now.

The fix is in the app, so the runtime on the phone is rebuilt as soon as the app is updated. Nothing to import for this one.

releases.name: 0.20.5 - Balance, Bugfixes
releases.body:
# MHGU Recomp 0.20.5

- Added optional "Rebalanced" preset to the monster HP scaling settings
    - This makes monster health scaling closer to what it is in newer-gen titles, like MH Rise (easier for 1 player, harder for 3-4 players)
    - This is *not* the default setting and probably never will be. You have to click the "Rebalanced" preset to use it. You can switch back by clicking "Original" at any time
    - In multiplayer hubs, the hub host's setting is always used. You do not need to change your settings to match the host, it will temporarily change automatically until you leave the hub
    - The reason for this preset is that the game is a slog in solo hub, but gets quite easy with 3-4 players and hunts are over very fast. I recommend you try it out! You might like it.
- Fixed a bug in GU where Bowgun critical distance changes at higher framerates, resulting in damage loss for bowguns
- Fixed a bug in GU where certain monster melee attacks "miss" the player more often at higher framerates (because of hitboxes not staying active long enough) 

Thanks a lot to the issue reporters and people who helped me with research for the high framerate bugs! (#23)

releases.name: 0.20.4 - Deviant Quests Shared, Bugfixes
releases.body:
# MHGU Recomp 0.20.4

- Added setting to share credit for clearing Deviant Quests! That means everyone gets credit for clearing the quest, not just the poster. This should make Deviant Quests a lot more enjoyable when playing with groups
    - This setting is enabled by default
    - This only clears quests that you "should" have access to. If your friend is 1 quest ahead and you complete that Deviant quest together, it will not count retroactively (as with village quests in the hub)
- Added support for Switch 2 Pro Controllers
- (Android) Added rumble for devices that have controller rumble but report that they don't (like the AYN Thor)
    - If you are playing this on your phone, this likely means that your phone will vibrate! You can turn off rumble in the *ingame* main menu options if it's annoying
- Weapon icons for unknown weapon types (like modded weapons) now show up as a large red "X" in the Search Hubs list and in the hub player list, instead of a Greatsword icon

- Made most mods load and perform *much* faster, particularly large content-adding mods

releases.name: v0.1.2 — Adreno 8xx graphics, lighter cloth physics, menu arrows
releases.body:
**Still a very early test build.** Install it over the previous version: saves and settings stay.

### Fixes
- **Adreno 8xx (810, 825, 830, 840, ...)**: Turnip now draws in a safer mode (system memory) on all of them, for the graphics glitches reported on the Adreno 830.
- **Less CPU load**: the cloth simulation (coats, jackets) took about a third of the CPU. It is now much cheaper: fewer solver iterations on low and medium "Game graphics" (low 2, medium 3, high keeps the game's 5) and faster code. Less heat on long sessions.

### New
- **Menu arrows**: on-screen up/down/left/right buttons in the menus, so you don't have to steer the cursor.

### Reporting bugs: logs are required
Please attach **both** `mafia2-native.log` and `app_process64_d3d9.log` from `Android/data/com.mafia2re.game/files/`, plus your phone model. Reports without logs can't be fixed. The issue form asks for them.

### Known issues
- Phones with old CPU cores only (Cortex-A53/A73, e.g. Snapdragon 625/660/665) are not supported.
- Mali GPUs with Vulkan 1.1 drivers can't run it; low-end GPUs (e.g. Mali-G57) are too slow.

1. Copy the game's `pc` and `edit` folders to `Internal storage/Android/data/com.mafia2re.game/files/game` (or to `Internal storage/Mafia II`).
2. Next to them, a `physx` folder with `PhysXCore_283.dll` and `NxCooking_283.dll` from the PhysX installer in the game's `Redist` folder.
3. Install the APK and start it.

Language: the game runs in the language of your files. With a Russian copy you can add:
- English text and speech: the `pc/sds_en` folder of an English install next to `pc/sds_ru`, then "Game language: English" in the settings;
- English speech with Russian text: the fan pack's `sds_ru` folder as `pc/sds_ru_en`, then "Voice: English".
The DLC episodes keep the language of their own files.
